english.legislation: Contrary to section 103I(1) and (3) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies from the 28th November 2022 due to changes made by the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. For the offence applying after this date relating to attempted breaches of SHPO's see H101095. For the offence relating to attempted breaches of SOPO's and foreign travel orders etc, see H101099.
(ii) Where a person is convicted of an offence under this section, it is not open to the court by or before which the person is convicted to make, in respect of the offence, an order for conditional discharge.
(iii) This offence relates to a breach of an SHPO made under sections 103A to 103k of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.
(iv) For breaches of SHPOs made under section 345 of the Sentencing Act 2020, see offence H22097 applying before the 29th November 2022 and offence H101107 applying from that date.

other.penalty:
Either way -Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictable: maximum 5 years imprisonment.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction increased from 2nd May 2022, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date, see section 282(4). For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months.
